description:
FILED s449r (Opus round-7 agent R).  #530 stays OPEN; this records the
measurement and the attempt so the next session does not repeat it.

THE BUG (unchanged, re-probed s449r vs perl 5.40.3):

    open(G, "<", $f) or die;
    my $s = G;          # perl: "G"     PCL: unbound variable G, crash
    print "x" . G;      # perl: xG      PCL: crash
    my @l = (G, 1);     # perl: G 1     PCL: crash
    print "", (G eq "G");   # perl: 1   PCL: crash
    $s .= G;            # perl: G       PCL: crash

`Pl::ExprToCL::gen_leaf`'s Word branch returns `_fh_designator($content)` --
the CL SYMBOL -- for any name in `Pl::Environment`'s filehandle registry,
because the handle SLOTS want a symbol (`%p-fh-arg` quotes it).  Outside a
slot nothing turns it back into the string perl reads.

THE ATTEMPT (measured, then reverted -- do not retry it as written):
mark the Word `_bareword_string` at the registry exit in
`Pl::PExpr::handle_subcalls` (~line 3860 -- the marker `gen_leaf` already
honours for every other unplaceable bareword) and CLEAR the mark in
`_read_star_slot_bareword`'s builtin half, i.e. let the SLOT claim it back.
The five crashes above became SAME with perl.  But corpus-diff went from
IDENTICAL to 4 of 111 files differing plus 2 of 6 shapes files, and every one
of those diffs is a HANDLE SLOT that lost its symbol:

    (p-chdir H)      -> (p-chdir "H")        perl-tests/chdir.t
    (p-pipe READ WRITE) -> (p-pipe "READ" "WRITE")   closure.t
    (p-open try â¦) (p-print :fh 'try) (p-close try) -> the string  eval.t
    (p-open of "harness") -> (p-open "of" "harness") flip.t
    (p-tell NAMED)   -> (p-tell "NAMED")     shapes/bareword-handles.pl
    (p-open |ï¼¦ï¼¨| â¦) -> (p-open "ï¼¦ï¼¨" â¦)    shapes/interpolation-nonascii.pl

because `_read_star_slot_bareword` does not reach them: it fires only at the
two funcall sites, only for a prototype whose first param is `*`, and only for
an ALL-CAPS name (`fh_bareword_shape`) -- `try`, `of` and `chdir`'s `H` fail
one test or another.

WHY NO SITE CAN DECIDE LOCALLY (the finding): at the registry exit the token
run for `close(G)` is `G` alone and the run for `my $s = G` is `G` alone; the
run for `pipe(READ, WRITE)` is `READ , WRITE` and the run for `(G, 1)` is
`G , 1`.  The two are indistinguishable there -- the discriminator is the
PARENT (which argument slot of which call), which that scan does not have.

THE THREE WAYS OUT, in the order they look cheapest:
 (a) the funcall ARG-LOOP override, the mechanism #594 used: a table
     func -> handle-slot indices, driven by the ~30 `%p-fh-arg` macro slots in
     cl/pcl-runtime.lisp (open, close, eof, binmode, seek, sysseek, read,
     sysread, syswrite, truncate, tell, getc, fileno, -t, opendir, readdir,
     closedir, rewinddir, pipe (2 slots), socket, bind, connect, listen,
     accept (2), shutdown, send, recv, getsockname, getpeername, setsockopt,
     getsockopt, socketpair (2)).  A second copy of a runtime fact -- the
     smell test says find the shared point first.
 (b) make the leaf emit the same spelling EVERYWHERE and teach the runtime.
     A QUOTED symbol `'G` already works in every handle slot (`%p-fh-arg`
     passes a quoted designator through untouched -- that is #491's qualified
     path), so the emission could be uniform; what it costs is that
     `to-string` of a symbol must become the perl NAME (it is the SBCL
     princ spelling today, i.e. case-INVERTED: "g").
 (c) answer it in the operand grammar with #266/#495 -- the ruled home for
     "what does a bare WORD mean in operand position".

BAR when it is next attempted: the five probes above, the inverses (every
handle slot in Pl/t/print-fh-magic-01.t and the six corpus/shapes files listed
here), corpus-diff, the 1036-file A/B, and the full sweep (this is the leaf
emitter, so nothing is local).
subject: #530 ATTEMPTED AND BACKED OUT (s449r): a registered bareword handle read outside a handle slot needs the "which argument slots are HANDLE slots" question answered ONCE -- no site can answer it from a token run
